record_type_quote: The present study provides a direct replication of early foundational research and extends prior work by incorporating constructs that have received limited systematic examination in this context, including locus of control.

targets.authors: Ngo, A. , Petrides K. V., and Vernon P. A.
targets.title: To Vaccinate or Not to Vaccinate? The Role of Personality.
targets.evidence_quote: Previous research found that individuals who support COVID‐19 vaccination, referred to as “Vaxxers,” scored higher on the traits of honesty‐humility and conscientiousness (Ngo et al. 2023). In contrast, those opposed to vaccination, or “Anti‐vaxxers,” scored higher on Dark Triad traits narcissism and Machiavellianism (Ngo et al. 2023). Our objective was to replicate these findings, and to explore additional traits, which may differ between these groups.
targets.outcome_quote: Ngo et al. (2023) found that individuals who are strongly opposed to vaccination (“Anti‐vaxxers”) scored higher on Dark Triad traits Machiavellianism and narcissism. In contrast, we found that there were no significant differences between the groups after applying a Bonferroni correction.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The named original personality differences were not significant after the authors’ correction; conscientiousness was nonsignificant even without correction. Significant conspiracy-belief and uncertainty differences are extensions and do not rescue the replication of the original targeted traits.
